unharnessed.meaning: Every beat survives: the ad, Andy's mermaid line, the five-dollar rule, Zeke's liniment death. "a five-dollar note and a cigar couldn't fix" and "there was this widow we roped in" keep the facts; additions are colour only.
unharnessed.sense: Terms fit: "lurk" for graft, "building society mortgage" for building and loan, "given away them ideas" (quit), "strife with the coppers", "she looked workable and decent enough".
unharnessed.authenticity: Mostly natural: "a good hard squiz at the city by-laws", "come sniffing round our agency", "pretty bloody well". The ad keeps US "realizes" and "rejigging his thinking" is a touch forced.
unharnessed.register: A steady level-3 retelling: idiom throughout ("knocked up an ad", "caper") without becoming a pub yarn; one "bloody", within dad vulgarity.
unharnessed.tone: Jeff's mock-learned con-man voice survives: "So far, so pernicious", "the perfidiousness of women", "hereditaments and appurtenances set out in the catalogue and writ of errors".
unharnessed.flow: Reads easily aloud: "there she was, same cottage, same sunflowers, same roosters perched on the washtub."
unharnessed.variety: Good spread ("squiz", "strife", "sloshed", "front up"), though "caper" appears four times and "lurk" twice.
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably O. Henry's Jeff Peters: the malapropisms ("perfidiousness", "pernicious") and legal parody are kept, retold in Aussie.

engine.meaning: Mostly the original verbatim, so facts survive, but "a five quid bill" changes the currency mid-story while "$6,000" stays, and "she looked a goer" shifts "feasible".
engine.sense: "she looked a goer" (of a widow, reads as sexually keen), "$3,000 dosh" and "invest dosh" strain in a formal ad, "a five quid bill" mixes forms.
engine.authenticity: Stage-Australian: swearing and swaps bolted onto untouched prose: "reconstructing his bloody mind", "our bloody agency", "Bugger me, as partners or coeducators", "Bloody hell, we had about $6,000".
engine.register: Largely untranslated ("said I", "As I have told you before") with a few token swaps ("nippers", "dosh", "staying back"); far lighter than level 3 in substance.
engine.tone: Where untouched the wry tone holds ("So far, so pernicious"), but the inserted "Bloody hell" and "Bugger me" jar against Jeff's mock-polished diction.
engine.flow: Clunky joins: "a roll as bloody big as the little end of a wagon tongue", "possessing $3,000 dosh", "a five quid bill".
engine.essence: Recognisably the original since it is mostly the original text: "hereditaments and appurtenances set forth in the catalogue and writ of errors" survives.

yarn.meaning: Complete and accurate in the main, but "the two-facedness of women" and "So far, so crooked" replace Jeff's ironic malapropisms with literal words, and "handed over on the spot" narrows "producible".
yarn.sense: Mostly exact ("offsiders", "front of the beak", "staying back at work"), but "she looked a goer" invites the wrong reading of a widow.
yarn.authenticity: Natural and local: "calm as you like but fair narked", "rearranging his noggin", "knocking back a bottle", "a treat". A few stock add-ons ("as far as you can chuck 'em").
yarn.register: A full level-3 retelling, even the ad: "has $3,000 in hard dosh"; vulgarity nil, within the brief.
yarn.tone: Wry and roguish throughout, though plainer words ("So far, so crooked", "bits and pieces and goods and chattels") soften the mock-legal pomposity.
yarn.flow: Smooth mostly; "or else end up front of the beak" drops a word, and the chattels list is a pile-up.
yarn.variety: Broad range ("offsiders", "narked", "noggin", "sozzled") but "lurk" four times and "dosh" three.
yarn.essence: Clearly the story, but the malapropism humour that defines Jeff's voice is partly flattened ("two-facedness", "crooked").

unharnessed.why: "caper" is leaned on for every scheme (four uses).
The ad is left verbatim with US spelling "realizes"; fine as a quoted document but untouched.
Slightly stiff; loses the comic formality without much gain.

engine.why: Bolted-on "bloody" in a slot no Australian would put it.

engine.quote: Bugger me, as partners or coeducators
engine.why: Exclamation pasted into an otherwise formal sentence.
Slang dropped into the stiff ad wording; reads as a word swap.
Mixes British/Aussie unit with US "bill"; inconsistent with retained dollar sums.
Of a widow "a goer" reads as sexually willing, not workable.

engine.quote: As I have told you before," said Jeff Peters
engine.original: As I have told you before," said Jeff Peters
engine.why: Most of the text is left untranslated, far under level 3.

yarn.why: Loses Jeff's comic misuse of a big word; the joke depends on the wrong-word irony.
"a goer" about a woman suggests sexual willingness, not suitability.

yarn.quote: end up front of the beak
yarn.original: hereafter be held by a justice of the peace

yarn.quote: with or without the beauty and all the bits and pieces and goods and chattels
yarn.original: with or without the beauty, hereditaments and appurtenances
yarn.why: Stacked synonyms; loses the legal-jargon parody.

yarn.quote: a marriage lurk with no marriage in it
yarn.original: a matrimonial scheme that had no matrimony in it

summaries.unharnessed: A natural, complete level-3 retelling that keeps Jeff's voice and malapropisms; only some reliance on "caper".
summaries.engine: Mostly the untouched original with "bloody" and "dosh" bolted on; under-translated and stagey.
summaries.yarn: Lively, idiomatic and complete, but trades Jeff's malapropisms for plain words and uses "a goer" loosely.
